scope.quote: gHYBR mints too few shares on deposit by using post-deposit totalAssets, causing systematic depositor value loss

The `GovernanceHYBR.deposit()` function calculates shares using `totalAssets()` that already includes the new deposit, resulting in systematic under-minting of shares to depositors. The function adds HYBR to the veNFT (increasing `totalAssets`) before calling `calculateShares()`, causing the share calculation to use an inflated denominator. This transfers value from new depositors to existing shareholders on every single deposit.
The `GovernanceHYBR` contract implements a vault system where users deposit HYBR and receive gHYBR shares representing proportional ownership. The fundamental accounting principle for vaults is:
1. First depositing HYBR into the veNFT (increasing `totalAssets`)
2. Then calculating shares using the already-increased `totalAssets`
This causes the denominator in the share calculation to be inflated, resulting in fewer shares minted than the depositor deserves.
